newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Email sees stronger second half.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Email sees stronger second half.

text.p: Appliance and building products manufacturer Email Ltd said on Monday its expects its second half profit to be well ahead of the first half.
Email said the environment for industrial activities remained difficult and recent economic forecasts had deferred the timing of an upturn in the economic drivers relevant to the company.

"Nevertheless the significant improvements in the company's pre-tax operating profits flowing from restructuring across the 12 months, are expected to continue in the second half," it said in a statement accompanying half year results.
"As well there should be the normal lift in sales and margins, leading to a second half profit well ahead of the first half," the company said.
Chairman Peter Cottrell said the 34 percent rise in pre-tax operating profit was encouraging, with profits and margins improving in all operating groups except industrial products.
Improvements in major appliances and building products were achieved on reduced sales in markets which deteriorated further in the period, he said.
Industrial products was down because of sharply lower sales and margins, reflecting lower activity in markets it services.
Email said borrowings at the end of the half were A$377.5 million, down A$76.3 million since March. This was partly due to a A$50 million securitisation program for the metals group.
Email said a A$5.78 million abnormal loss before tax was mainly due to reducing overhead structures.
The first half dividend was reduced to 8.0 cents a share fully franked from 11.5 cents last year.

Email said the dividends were realigned with the normal patterns of profit, with the second half traditionally much stronger, in light of continuing uncertainty in the areas of the economy in which the company operates.
Interest costs were higher due to Atlas Steels, acquired in November 1995 for A$130 million.
Email said in the metals group sales and profits were both well above the previous corresponding period, largely due to the inclusion of Atlas.
Sheet and coil business Alloy Steel, acquired in September, was trading well and would provide synergies with Union Steel and Atlas, it said.
In major appliances, sales were lower in weaker markets, but profits were well ahead due to cost reductions in all areas, particularly the Orange and Adelaide plants.
Email said the residential housing market had yet to show signs of improvement, but the building products group performance was much better on lower sales.
A restructuring of operations started last year had provided major benefits, it said.
Industrial products had a difficult half year, and depressed market conditions meant a cutback in operations.
In air conditions and heat transfer, an overhang in inventory from last year's poor summer conditions had led to price discounting, the company said.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
